title: Starting and Ending Sentences
keyIdea: Every sentence starts with a capital letter and ends with a mark. A telling sentence (a statement) ends with a full stop. An asking sentence (a question) ends with a question mark. A sentence that shows surprise, a big feeling or a shout ends with an exclamation mark. When two ideas are squashed together, put a full stop after the first one and a capital letter at the start of the next.

kid: A sentence starts with a big letter. It is called a capital letter. The cat sat on the mat. See the big T?
A sentence ends with a mark. It shows the idea is done. A dot is called a full stop. Put it after the last word, not in the middle.

Some sentences ask. Can you see the moon? Asking ends with a question mark. Telling ends with a full stop. Some shout or feel big. What a big cake this is! Ouch, that hurts! These end with an exclamation mark.
Two ideas need two sentences. We went to the park. We fed the ducks. Stop after park. Then start with a capital.
adult: This is sentence demarcation. In England's National Curriculum, Year 1 pupils begin to punctuate sentences using a capital letter and a full stop, question mark or exclamation mark, and use a capital letter for names and the pronoun I. Year 2 adds the four sentence forms: statement, question, exclamation and command. US Common Core L.K.2 and L.1.2 ask for the same capitals and end punctuation.

Teach the marks by what the sentence does, not by its length. A statement tells, a question asks and needs an answer, and an exclamation shows strong feeling or surprise. In the grammar tests used in England, an exclamation sentence starts with What or How and has a verb, as in What a big cake this is! Short cries such as Ouch! and commands such as Stop! may also take an exclamation mark.

Common mistakes: no capital at the start, a capital in the middle of a sentence, a full stop at the end of a line rather than at the end of the idea, a full stop on a question, and two ideas run together with no full stop. Another slip is reading What a big cake this is as a question because it starts with What.

In the lab your child taps the first word to give it a capital, drags a full stop to the end of the idea, picks a full stop, question mark or exclamation mark by how each sentence sounds, and splits squashed lines into two sentences.

familyTip: When you read together, stop at each full stop and take a breath, and make your voice go up at a question mark. Then ask your child: how should this one end?

practice.prompt: Which sentence is written the right way?
practice.hint: Look at the first letter and the very end.
practice.explain: The dog ran fast. starts with a capital T and ends with a full stop, so it is right.

practice.prompt: Ali writes {a} telling sentences and {b} asking sentences. How many question marks does he need?
practice.hint: Only the asking sentences end with a question mark.
practice.explain: Only the {b} asking sentences need a question mark. The {a} telling ones end with full stops. So he needs {b}.

practice.prompt: Which mark ends this sentence? What a huge cake that is
practice.hint: Is it asking something, or showing surprise?
practice.explain: It starts with What, but it does not ask. It shows surprise, so it ends with an exclamation mark !

practice.prompt: Mia writes {n} sentences. How many capital letters does she need at the start of her sentences?
practice.hint: Every sentence starts with one capital letter.
practice.explain: Each sentence starts with one capital letter, so {n} sentences need {n} capitals at the start.

pool.prompt: What goes at the start of every sentence?
pool.hint: Think of the big T in The cat sat on the mat.
pool.explain: Every sentence starts with a capital letter. The marks go at the end.

pool.prompt: Which mark ends this sentence? Can you see the bird
pool.hint: Does it tell, ask or shout?
pool.explain: Can you see the bird asks something, so it ends with a question mark ?

pool.prompt: Where does the full stop go? I like red apples
pool.hint: The full stop goes where the idea is finished.
pool.explain: After apples, the last word. I like. is not a finished idea, so a full stop after like is too soon.

pool.prompt: Which line has two sentences written the right way?
choices: It was hot. We had ice cream.
It was hot we had ice cream.
It was hot. we had ice cream.
pool.hint: Each idea needs a full stop and the next one a capital letter.
pool.explain: It was hot. We had ice cream. has a full stop after hot and a capital W for the new sentence.

pool.prompt: Which mark ends this sentence? Help, the boat is sinking
pool.hint: How would you say it if it were true?
pool.explain: Help, the boat is sinking is a shout with a big feeling, so it ends with an exclamation mark !

pool.prompt: A story has {a} telling sentences, {b} questions and 1 exclamation. How many full stops does it have?
pool.hint: Questions get ? and the exclamation gets !. Only telling sentences end with a full stop.
pool.explain: Only the {a} telling sentences end with a full stop, so there are {a} full stops.

pool.prompt: Sam wrote {n} sentences. He forgot the capital letter on 1 of them. How many sentences start the right way?
pool.hint: Take away the one with no capital letter.
pool.explain: {n} take away 1 is {=n-1}, so {=n-1} sentences start with a capital letter.

pool.prompt: Which word needs a capital letter? the dog ate my hat.
pool.hint: Which word comes first? The first word gets the capital.
pool.explain: the is the first word, so it needs a capital: The dog ate my hat.
